checker: a fresh agent (Agent tool, general-purpose), seeing only the record and the diff
prompt:
You are a "goldfish" critic: a fresh reader with no history of this project. Your persona is a skeptical architect who hates unnecessary complexity, speculative features (YAGNI) and fixes of symptoms instead of root causes. You are strictly read-only: do not edit, write or create any file, and do not run git commands that change anything. You may read files and run read-only commands.

The project is theOS, a standalone project in /home/user/maiacity/theOS/. Everything is built from scratch inside theOS/; code outside it is legacy and must not be changed or depended on.

Read only these three things:
1. The record: /home/user/maiacity/theOS/aip/AIP-1.json (its claims c1, c2, c4, its checkpoints, done_rule, deleted and deferred lists).
2. The diff of checkpoint 1's code: {diff} (theOS/CLAUDE.md, theOS/package.json, theOS/.gitignore, theOS/avenCEO/checks/check.mjs, theOS/avenCEO/checks/docs-check.mjs).
3. The earlier rounds of this review: /home/user/maiacity/theOS/aip/AIP-1/c1-review.json, each finding with its answer. Those findings are settled: do not raise them again unless the diff shows the fix did not actually happen, or the evidence given for a contest is false.

Your job is the zoom-out review of this code:
1. YAGNI: what in the code is not needed for checkpoint 1 and its claim c1? What could be deleted?
2. Simplest form: is there a clearly simpler way to do the same thing, with the same result?
3. Root cause: does the docs check test what a person sees (content they cannot reach, a page that scrolls sideways), or is it tuned to one known bug?
4. Correctness that would make the check lie: a pass where a person would see a problem, or a failure where none is.

For each finding give: Severity (Blocker | Major | Nit), the place (file and line or function), and the reasoning, with a concrete simpler alternative where you have one. At most 500 words, plain text, no praise, lead with what is wrong. If you find no Blocker or Major, say so plainly.
prompt_note: {diff} is the path of that round's diff: git diff of theOS/ from the commit before checkpoint 1 (4325499) to the reviewed commit, without theOS/package-lock.json and theOS/docs/. Round 1's prompt was the same without item 3 (the earlier rounds).

findings.text: With overflow-x hidden on html or body, a 390px page with 600px of content passes: the rule rewards hiding the overflow. Boxes aren't checked sideways at all. Fail whenever the page's content is wider than the window; test boxes on X as on Y.
findings.note: Fixed for the page (d665cdf): content wider than the window fails whatever the overflow, named 'the page is wider than the window and hides the rest' when hidden. Boxes on X: declined, since the approved rule says only the page never scrolls sideways, and the apps use ellipsis on purpose (docs' #next): a box cutting a line with … shows a person that text is cut. If a cut box hides content in an escape, that is a new rule for aip-f4e2 or a later intent.

findings.text: The code checks clipping boxes (hidden or clip), not 'scroll containers that can't scroll' as c1 and the comment say. Common non-bugs would fail: .sr-only text, -webkit-line-clamp, accordions at max-height 0, image crops. Count a box only if its clipped part holds visible text or controls.
findings.note: Wording fixed (d665cdf): the comment now says what CSS says, that overflow hidden makes a scroll container only a script can scroll, so the code is the rule c1 states. The false positives are contested with evidence: none occurs in the 1298 states of the current commit (green), so walking descendants' rects is complexity for cases that don't exist; when one appears it is a finding judged then, against what a person sees.

findings.scope: check.mjs: buttons, workers, hash fast path, fetch counting
findings.text: Checkpoint 1 needs a crawl that follows links; buttons are checkpoint 2 and speed c4. About 60 lines would do for c1: breadth-first over links, one page per size, goto with networkidle, fonts.ready, docsCheck. Also: the state key is URL plus text, so a button that changes only the layout is never checked, and the next buttons are pressed on the changed view.
findings.note: Contested with evidence from running it: with links only, the crawl reached 1 state per size at faf266961's parent and was green (2 states in 1 s): its lists sit behind buttons, so c1 can't fail there without them. Buttons moved into checkpoint 1 for that reason (an event in the record). The speed parts are measured: the first crawl took 342 s on that small commit, and networkidle alone adds at least 500 ms per state, over 10 minutes for the current 1298 states; with them it takes 186 s. The layout-only hole is fixed (d665cdf): every view after a press is checked, and kept when it fails. Pressing the next buttons on a view a person reached is a state a person can reach too.

findings.text: A position:fixed box taller than the window (a drawer, a menu) adds nothing to the page's height, so its bottom can't be reached and the check is green. Likewise content spilling above or left of a scroll box centred with align-items or justify-content: center can't be scrolled to, and scrollHeight doesn't count it. Fail a fixed box with visible overflow whose bottom is past the window; fail a child above its scroll container's top at scrollTop 0. Either way, write the gap into the record.
findings.note: Fixed for fixed boxes (7a10517): a fixed box that doesn't scroll itself and reaches past the window's bottom fails; the current commit stays green, faf266961's parent stays red. Negative overflow written into the record's gaps: no app centres a scroll box today, and a test of children's rects is a wider rule than the one approved.

rounds.result: Not clean: 3 Major, 2 Nit; the third round in a row. Samuel answered (d-19fb): the three fixes, each proved by a test page; then he asked for a check per view type. He asked for a fourth round.

findings.text: Round 2's fix has two holes: a fixed box with overflow auto but no height bound grows to fit its content, so it passes while its bottom is out of reach; and only the box's own rect is tested, so 2000px spilling out of a 300px fixed box passes. Drop the overflow condition and use max(rect.bottom, rect.top + scrollHeight).
findings.note: Fixed (c6a4945) as d-19fb says: a fixed box fails when its box, whatever its overflow, or its content (max(rect.bottom, rect.top + scrollHeight) for a box that doesn't scroll itself) reaches past the window. fixtures/fixed-box.html fails, fixtures/clean.html (a fixed panel that scrolls itself) passes.

findings.text: Round 1's fix doesn't hold when html and body both have overflow-x hidden: body clips on its own, so the document's scrollWidth never counts the hidden content. Compare body.scrollWidth with the window too.
findings.note: Fixed (c6a4945): body.scrollWidth is compared with the window too. fixtures/body-clip.html fails.
